summary: The candidate is a verified partial correction: it fixes the reproduced AITER bf16-output-store violation, centralizes the GEMM implementation, and migrates the five architectures named by the prior review. It does not complete the original issue's universal RouterGate consolidation because multiple issue-relevant consumers retain model-local gate implementations and do not all inherit the shared fp32-output and deterministic dispatch policy.

tests.what_was_measured: On MI350X at M=1,7,8,15,16,17,64, every fp32-typed output exactly equaled the independent CPU fp32 reference rounded through bf16 and was exactly bf16-representable. Maximum error against the unrounded fp32 reference was 0.191894531, reproducing the output-store contract failure.
At the exact candidate, all boundary-shape outputs were fp32 and not bf16-representable. Maximum error against the independent CPU fp32 matmul was 7.62939453e-06.
Four candidate regression tests passed: fp32 reference/output contract, fp32-compute and correction-bias behavior, deterministic small-token bypass, and neutral/legacy import identity.

Independent MI350X adversarial test forced router-GEMV and tiny-GEMM probes to raise under deterministic inference. Neither path was consulted; the output was fp32, not bf16-representable, and within 9.5367431640625e-07 of the CPU fp32 reference.

tests.what_was_measured: Confirmed the five prior-review architectures use RouterGate, but also confirmed remaining issue-relevant local gates in Kimi Linear, Bailing-MoE, Bailing-MoE-Linear, LLaDA2, Bailing-MoE-v3, and a DeepSeek-v2 wrapper.

gpu_execution.evidence: One AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx95) under Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 executed the failing-before and passing-candidate numerical tests plus the independent deterministic-dispatch adversarial test. Raw logs are in reports/j-103aabf2d33f/raw/.

remaining_counterexamples: Kimi Linear still constructs its router with ReplicatedLinear and therefore does not use the shared RouterGate policy; the candidate changes only its correction-bias dtype.

Bailing-MoE and Bailing-MoE-Linear retain model-local BailingMoEGate implementations. Removing their explicit output downcast is a valid precision fix, but their output dtype and dispatch remain controlled locally rather than by RouterGate.
LLaDA2 retains a model-local LLaDA2MoeGate. Removing its explicit output downcast does not consolidate it behind RouterGate or give it the shared deterministic/small-token policy.
Bailing-MoE-v3 retains a model-local gate wrapper. It calls shared helper functions, but it is still outside the proposed single gate layer.
DeepSeek-v2 retains a model-local MoEGate wrapper for AMX and extended call signatures. It reuses the shared helpers but is not fully consolidated into RouterGate.

Many additional MoE model files still use ReplicatedLinear or other local router implementations, as recorded by the candidate's own all_router_consumers_after.txt; those consumers were not migrated or validated under one policy.
remaining_limitations: No model weights were available, so full-model checkpoint compatibility, semantic accuracy, serving behavior, and performance were not tested.
CUDA-only tiny GEMM, DeepGEMM, HPC-Ops, AMX, NPU, XPU, distributed, NVIDIA, and non-gfx95 paths were unavailable on the assigned AMD MI350X and remain unverified.
No native source changed in the candidate and repository-environment.json declares no native build target, so native rebuild was not applicable.
The AITER removal's performance impact was not benchmarked.
